source_review.notes: Checked all ten references. Current POSIX.1-2024 semaphore definition, wait, timed-wait, and post semantics; Java SE 26 Semaphore permit, fairness, bulk, and memory-consistency behavior; and the current Go memory-model channel synchronization rules were verified against official specifications.

evidence: Reviewed capacity K, available permits S, checked-out multiset U, usable-resource set H, fairness order, bounds, and transition notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Permit accounting is consistently distinguished from physical resource health and scheduler policy.

evidence: Executed all 90 order-preserving histories for three acquire/release pairs and independently confirmed 54 capacity-two-safe histories, 36 rejected histories, and maximum admitted occupancy two.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The exact counts match the executable snippet expectations and the stated finite model.

evidence: Re-derived the acquire and release transition equations, conservation induction, bulk all-or-none requirement, and resize/drain accounting.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Every legal fixed-capacity transition preserves S plus U equals K under its explicit precondition.

evidence: Reviewed zero availability, impossible bulk request, partial hold-and-wait, failed try-acquire, timeout-success race, cancellation, exception, transfer, double release, health loss, unfair barging, resize, process crash, shutdown, and destruction.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Failure before acquisition creates no obligation; every terminal path after success releases or transfers exactly once.

evidence: Checked conservation, obligation ownership, physical-pool alignment, all-or-none bulk acquisition, separate queue bounds, API-scoped fairness and visibility, resize generations, and quiescent destruction.
invariant_checking.notes: Semaphore capacity is not overclaimed as mutex ownership, resource health, rate limiting, or lifecycle proof.

evidence: Reviewed the base case and inductive acquire/release steps, the illegal unmatched-release transition, and the two-job partial-acquisition deadlock argument.
proof_review.notes: Proof obligations and assumptions are explicit; safety and progress are treated separately.

evidence: Audited the language-neutral permit-guard schema, conservation derivation, fairness discussion, memory-order claims, and platform-specific lifecycle claims.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The schema is explicitly non-executable and API claims remain qualified by their named specifications.

evidence: Reproduced one executable Python result and confirmed the schematic block is intentionally skipped with a stated reason.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter explicitly disclaims real-thread execution, library implementation testing, weak-memory exploration, cancellation modeling, arbitrary-program proof, and safety-critical approval.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distinctions among permits, physical resources, mutex ownership, condition predicates, admission, rate, fairness, visibility, transfer, and resizing.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed connection pools, scoped permit tokens, weighted admission, bounded queues, deadline handling, cancellation cleanup, resource-health reconciliation, observability, process sharing, and shutdown.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter develops permit conservation from first principles through production lifecycle cases using ten distinct examples and five progressively demanding matched exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, aerospace, medical-device, clinical, controls, hardware, real-time, functional-safety, cybersecurity, certification, regulatory, or human-factors review is claimed. Finite enumeration and manual analysis do not prove a production semaphore implementation, fairness, timing, resource health, or safety-critical deployment fitness.
